title: Dataset/storage service: unified catalog + access API for all dataset consumers
description:
Datasets are the fundamental unit of mainframe storage interaction, and nearly every jackal component touches them — so dataset interaction should be ONE well-defined service that all consumers use, rather than each utility reaching into catalog internals + importing red-dragon drivers ad hoc. Build this FIRST; every os-runtime dataset feature (GDG, PDS, ESDS/RRDS, AIX, SORT, IEBGENER, IEBCOPY, DCB, concatenation) is a client of it.

CURRENT LEAK (the motivation): DatasetCatalog is the shared *catalog* API (resolve/allocate/dispose/delete_dsn), but (a) the *access* face is not an API — idcams/executor.py imports red-dragon IndexedDriver/SequentialDriver directly and opens them itself, while cobol_step takes catalog.allocate(dd).path and hands a raw Path to red-dragon's RealFileIOProvider (which uses the SAME drivers internally). Two consumers, two ways to reach a dataset's bytes. (b) allocate_ksds bakes one org into the catalog -> would sprawl to allocate_esds/rrds/pds/gdg.

TARGET (two clean faces, mirroring z/OS catalog + DADSM + access methods):
- CATALOG/BINDING face: resolve DSN->Dataset; allocate BY ORG (generalize allocate_ksds -> allocate(spec)); DISP lifecycle; GDG generation resolution; PDS member resolution. The parenthesized qualifier (gen/member) arrives structurally from the JCL grammar (no regex).
- ACCESS face: open-for-read / open-for-write by org -> a record reader/writer, wrapping red-dragon's drivers as the single access API. IDCAMS REPRO, SORT, IEBGENER all read/write through this instead of importing drivers.

CONSUMER-DRIVEN PRINCIPLE (binding instruction): the interfaces must be validated as consumable by EVERY consumer before they are fixed — IDCAMS (binding + access), COBOL steps (binding-ONLY; access is internal to the red-dragon VM via RealFileIOProvider), the runner DD allocate/dispose lifecycle, IEFBR14, and the forward consumers SORT/IEBGENER/IEBCOPY/GDG/PDS/ESDS/RRDS/AIX/DCB/concat. Build a consumer's slice against the API and adjust the API to fit, rather than designing it in isolation.

Constraints: FP/frozen, no None defaults, no defensive guards (fail loud), no regex. Brainstorm -> spec -> plan -> subagent-driven execution. This epic is a sibling to jackal-1o2 (JCL coverage), not a child — its own line of work.
notes:
SUBSTRATE AUDIT (2026-06-25) — design inputs from auditing red-dragon's file drivers + the CobolIOProvider seam:

THE ACCESS-API CONTRACT ALREADY EXISTS: interpreter/cobol/file_drivers.py defines FileOrganizationDriver — a runtime_checkable Protocol with a uniform, OPERATION-COMPLETE method set: open/close/read_seq/read_key/start(browse)/write/rewrite/delete. jackal-vxb's access face should ADOPT/re-export this Protocol as its contract, NOT invent a new one. The 'implicit surface' is FileOrganizationDriver (the Protocol) — NOT RealFileIOProvider (which is merely red-dragon's COBOL *adapter*: it maps VM __cobol_* calls onto a driver; it's the reference shape for jackal's own CobolIOProvider).

DECOUPLING: driver logic is clean (depends only on Path, OpenMode enum, IOResult dataclass; no VM/executor/ASG) and is already used standalone by jackal/idcams/executor.py. ONE WRINKLE: IOResult is defined in io_provider.py, which does 'from interpreter.vm.vm import Operators' — so importing a driver transitively pulls the VM. Benign for jackal (it runs the VM anyway), but the storage substrate is not truly VM-free. If a VM-independent dataset library is ever wanted, IOResult must move to a leaf module. Note for the spec, not a blocker.

COMPLETENESS: operation-complete (full CRUD + sequential + keyed + STARTBR positioning); ORG-partial. Present: PS (SequentialDriver), KSDS (IndexedDriver), RRDS (RelativeDriver — already there, so 1o2.21's RRDS half is substrate-ready; only ESDS is genuinely missing). Missing: ESDS, AIX, PDS members — these are NEW FileOrganizationDriver implementations (or member-routing for PDS) under the SAME Protocol, not a redesign.

IMPLICATION: jackal-vxb is 'consolidate + observe over a solid substrate', NOT 'build a storage engine'. Access face = pick driver by org -> add observability trace -> serve TWO client shapes (a CobolIOProvider adapter for VM-driven COBOL record I/O + status codes; direct Python calls for IDCAMS/SORT/IEBGENER). The CobolIOProvider injection seam (run(io_provider=...)) is how COBOL access plugs in -> COBOL becomes a FULLY-TRACED consumer (not binding-only), the observability-first payoff. Substrate (the 3 drivers) stays red-dragon's; jackal wraps, never reimplements.
RE-SCOPED (2026-06-25): the storage ENGINE (access + neutral outcomes) moved to a red-dragon epic (shared across the mainframe stack — see red-dragon docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-shared-access-method-engine-design.md). jackal-vxb is now JUST the jackal dataset CATALOG (DSN->dataset, DISP lifecycle, GDG generations, PDS members) that CONSUMES the red-dragon engine + maps neutral outcomes -> COBOL FILE STATUS. Observability/tracing deferred. This becomes actionable only after the red-dragon engine's first piece lands and is bumped in.

title: JCL parser via ANTLR grammar behind a Java bridge (proleap-bridge pattern); retire Lark
description: Foundation for thorough JCL coverage. ARCHITECTURE (decided): adopt a mature ANTLR4 JCL grammar in JAVA and call it from Python through a bridge, exactly like red-dragon's proleap-bridge does for COBOL — NOT a pure-Python ANTLR target. The bridge parses JCL (Java/ANTLR) and serializes a structured AST (JSON) back to Python; jackal deserializes into its EXISTING frozen model (Job/Step/DD/Disp). The hand-written Lark grammar (jackal/jcl/grammar.lark + Transformer) is retired. Candidate grammar: cschneid-the-elder/mapa (MIT) — bridge route means its embedded Java actions + symbolic-substitution + disposition analysis are REUSED, not stripped (the key advantage over pure-Python generation). Tasks: (1) spike — confirm mapa's JCL .g4 parses the real CardDemo jobs in Java; (2) stand up the bridge (extend proleap-bridge or a sibling jcl-bridge JAR; a JclSerializer -> JSON like StatementSerializer/AsgSerializer); (3) Python side calls the bridge via RealSubprocessRunner + bridge JAR (build product, like proleap), deserializes to the model; (4) migrate v2 features (in-stream, SYSOUT) + delete Lark; (5) re-green full suite + gated CardDemo e2e. RUNTIME: JVM per parse (already paid for COBOL). Attribution: keep upstream LICENSE/provenance.
design: Open design forks for the spec: (a) extend the EXISTING proleap-bridge JAR vs a SEPARATE jcl-bridge JAR; (b) mapa vs grossvater/jcl-parser as the grammar; (c) serialization contract (JSON shape) JCL-bridge -> Python. Must reproduce 100% of current Lark parse behavior (incl. in-stream/SYSOUT/the e2e jobs) before merge. Spike de-risks (a)/(b) before committing.
notes: SPIKE RESULT (2026-06-21): GO — grammar = cschneid-the-elder/mapa, MIT. JCL grammar at mapa/jcl/src/JCLParser.g4 (1002L) + JCLLexer.g4 (5096L), start rule 'startRule', tokenVocab=JCLLexer. ACTION-FREE (2 lexer-mode brace sites only) -> clean for a thin Java bridge. Coverage present: JOB/EXEC(PGM=/PROC=)/DD + per-param rules (DISP/DSN/SPACE/SYSOUT/UNIT/VOLUME/COND), in-stream (DD */DATA/DLM, grammar-native), DD concatenation, COND=, IF/ELSE/ENDIF, PROC/PEND + symbolics, GDG gen refs, referbacks (DSN=*.STEP.DD), JOBLIB/SYSCHK, OUTPUT, SET, INCLUDE, EXPORT. EVIDENCE: 38/38 CardDemo .jcl parse with ZERO errors via antlr4-parse (ANTLR 4.13.1); error detection verified on garbage. Column sensitivity (cols 73-80, // markers) handled INSIDE the lexer -> no 80-col pre-splitting needed. In-stream/SYSIN grammar-native -> no manual extraction. Separate JCLPP preprocessor grammar exists for symbolic/INCLUDE expansion — DESIGN FORK: parse raw structure (sufficient now; 38/38 was raw) vs run JCLPP first (needed for PROC/symbolics, 1o2.2). grossvater/jcl-parser REJECTED: Apache-2.0 but action-heavy, needs custom Java lexer, semantically weak (opaque FIELD_ID/params, no DISP/COND/GDG rules). Java glue needed: small — a main that runs lexer+parser and serializes the tree to JSON on stdout (proleap-bridge shape).
close_reason: Merged to main (9a7ec7d). JCL parsed via mapa ANTLR grammar behind jcl-bridge Java bridge; Lark retired; 42 tests green incl gated CardDemo e2e + parse-sweep (TRANBKP/DEFGDGB now parse). Malformed-JSON->JclParseError. Carried follow-ups (non-blocking): PROC= parsing untested (1o2.2), no Java unit test.

title: Generation Data Groups (GDG): relative + absolute generation refs
description: GDGs (DSN=A.B.C(+1), (0), (-1)) are pervasive for dated/cyclic batch datasets. Add a GDG base + generation model to the catalog: define a GDG base (IDCAMS DEFINE GDG or pre-seeded), resolve (+1)=new generation, (0)=current, (-n)=nth prior; roll generations on job completion per DISP. Without this, jobs referencing generation datasets fail to resolve DSNs.
design: Catalog gains a GDG registry mapping base -> ordered generation list; DSN resolution interprets the (gen) suffix at allocate time; (+1) allocations are cataloged on step/job success per normal disposition. Parse the (gen) suffix in the DSN grammar token, not regex.

title: Step-level conditional execution: COND= (RC-gated step bypass)
description: Steps currently always run regardless of prior return codes. Add JCL-level COND= on EXEC cards (and job-level COND=) to bypass steps based on prior step return codes: COND=(code,op[,stepname]) — bypass this step if 'code op RC' is true (operands reversed); multiple conditions COND=((c,op),(c,op)) bypass if ANY is true. CardDemo uses (0,NE) ('skip if any prior step failed') and (4,LT) pervasively. RC-only scope: no COND=EVEN/ONLY, no JCL IF/THEN/ENDIF (those are split to a sibling issue; IDCAMS-level IF/THEN already works). Runner gains per-step RC state; bypassed steps -> StepResult(ran=False).
design: Grammar: extend exec_card for COND=; add if_stmt/else/endif statements at the job level (Lark, no regex). Runner: maintain a step-RC map; evaluate conditions before dispatch; mark skipped steps in JobResult (ran=False, distinct from RC). COND= semantics are inverted ('bypass if true') — document carefully. IF/THEN is the modern, clearer form; COND= the legacy form — support both.
notes: ARCH-REVIEW CROSS-REF (2026-06-22): the whole-branch review of 1o2.9 independently flagged the same root issue this covers — cobol_step.py hardcodes StepResult return_code=0 (cobol_step.py:66), the runner never checks step RCs so a job never aborts on failure, and Disp.abnormal is modelled but dead (never consulted by catalog.dispose). All resolved by this issue's plan: wire real RETURN-CODE via read_return_code(vm), thread RC into step sequencing, and (for abnormal disp) branch dispose on step success/failure. The StepResult.ran->StepDisposition enum chosen here also addresses the review's boolean-blindness note.
close_reason: Merged to main. COND= conditional step execution: real COBOL RETURN-CODE (Part 1), Cond/CondOp model + StepDisposition, pure should_bypass (IBM reversed operands), bridge emits cond (execParmCOND/jobParmCOND), runner fold bypasses steps. 7 tasks subagent-driven, final review Ready-to-merge, full suite 71 green incl real-COBOL COND e2e. EVEN/ONLY+IF/THEN fail loud -> deferred to 1o2.8. Follow-up: jackal-449 (condFromWords silent catch).

title: Broaden jackal JCL execution coverage beyond the v2 vertical slice
description: jackal v2 proved one deep vertical slice (IDCAMS provision/load -> COBOL read, byte-faithful EBCDIC, real CardDemo ACCTFILE->READACCT). This epic broadens coverage toward 'understand/execute useful JCL'. STRATEGY CHANGE: rather than grow the hand-written Lark grammar feature-by-feature, ADOPT a mature reference ANTLR4 JCL grammar (candidate: cschneid-the-elder/mapa, MIT — already does symbolic substitution + dataset disposition) and GENERATE A PURE-PYTHON PARSER from it (ANTLR Python3 target: Java at build time, antlr4-python3-runtime at runtime; no JVM per parse). title: COBOL: pseudo-conversational reenter flag lost — DFHCOMMAREA reference-mod group-slice MOVE shifts bytes ~12
description:
Driving real CardDemo COACTVWC turn 5 (account-id entry) revealed the reenter gate never fires: COACTVWC always takes the CDEMO-PGM-ENTER first-display branch instead of CDEMO-PGM-REENTER, so 9000-READ-ACCT (the 3 VSAM reads) never executes.

ROOT CAUSE (COBOL-FRONTEND, silent data bug, no warning): the reenter flag CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT (PIC 9(01); 88 CDEMO-PGM-REENTER; defined in copybook COCOM01Y, nested 05 CDEMO-GENERAL-INFO then 10 CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) is at rel offset 33 of the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA. On entry COACTVWC copies the inbound commarea via a reference-modified group-slice MOVE of the DFHCOMMAREA linkage group into the WS CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, then EVALUATEs the 88-levels.

OBSERVED: after turn 4 the persisted commarea has the EBCDIC '1' (0xF1) flag at byte 45 instead of byte 33 -- a consistent ~12-byte shift, with the CDEMO-GENERAL-INFO header (bytes 0-32) blank. DECISIVE: hand-building a clean inbound commarea with the flag correctly at offset 33 STILL takes first-display -- so the inbound reference-modified group-slice MOVE mis-aligns the bytes (the slice writes/reads ~12 bytes off), and/or the nested 88-level evaluation reads the wrong byte. Simple isolated SET-88 + group ref-mod cases round-trip correctly, so the trigger is the reference-modified GROUP-slice MOVE over a LINKAGE/DFHCOMMAREA region combined with a deeply-nested-copybook 88-level.

REPRO: drive tests/integration/cics/test_carddemo_signon_real.py through a 5th turn (ACCTSID entry into COACTVWC) -- COACTVWC never RECEIVEs/READs. Likely minimal repro: a program with a COCOM01Y-style nested commarea, MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(1:len) TO group, then test the 88-level on a field at a non-zero nested offset.

LAYER: COBOL-FRONTEND (reference-modified group-slice MOVE materialization over LINKAGE / nested-group byte addressing). NOT core VM, NOT VSAM, NOT CICS-layer. Blocks every pseudo-conversational reenter flow.
close_reason: Root cause: ProLeap bridge serialized 'LENGTH OF <group>' inside a ref-mod expression as a bogus {kind:ref,name:'LENGTHOF...'} (getText glue) -> eval_ref_mod_expr resolved it to 0 -> ref-mod start/length collapsed, shifting bytes by LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA (12). Fixed: bridge serializeBasisCtx emits {kind:length_of}; ref_mod.py RefModLengthOf variant; lower_arithmetic resolves it to byte_length. COACTVWC reenter branch now fires -> reaches 9000-READ-ACCT. Commit 442179c1; full suite 14057 green.

title: BMS loader cannot parse real BMS macro source (continuation lines); extracts 0 maps from CardDemo, masked by test stubs
description:
interpreter/cics/bms/loader.py::_parse_bms_file is a minimal regex parser that extracts ZERO maps/fields from real BMS macro source. Verified: BmsLoader(maps_dir=aws-mainframe-carddemo/app/bms) -> maps loaded: []. The CICS integration/durable tests therefore register hand-fabricated STUB maps (register_stub) with invented contiguous offsets, masking that real BMS maps don't load.

ROOT CAUSES (multiple):
1. Continuation-line format: real BMS uses col-72 '-' continuations, so a single DFHMDF's params (ATTRB/COLOR/LENGTH/POS/INITIAL) span several physical lines. The regex (\w+)\s+DFHMDF\s+.*?POS=\((\d+),(\d+)\).*?LENGTH=(\d+) matches only within one line and in a FIXED order (POS before LENGTH). Real maps often put LENGTH before POS. -> no match -> 0 fields -> map never committed (if current_map and fields).
2. Multi-map mapsets: the parser iterates ALL DFHMDI (resetting fields each time) then SEPARATELY iterates ALL DFHMDF across the WHOLE file into one dict, assigning them to the LAST map only. A mapset with multiple DFHMDI maps is broken.
3. Unlabeled fields: literal/label-only DFHMDF (e.g. 'Tran :' prompt) have a blank name field; regex (\w+) would mis-bind to the next token.
4. Offset model is WRONG for the symbolic map: offset=(row-1)*80+(col-1) computes a 3270 SCREEN position. But the COBOL symbolic map (e.g. CACTVWAO/CACTVWAI from cpy-bms/COACTVW.CPY) lays fields out as sequential L(halfword)+A(attr)+data triplets, NOT screen positions. So even if fields parsed, the offsets wouldn't match what SEND/RECEIVE MAP reads/writes in working storage.
5. It is itself regex string-surgery (.upper() whole file + finditer) of the kind the project avoids.

DESIRED: a real BMS macro parser (handle col-72 continuations, DFHMSD/DFHMDI/DFHMDF with arbitrary param order, ATTRB/OCCURS/PICIN/PICOUT/GRPNAME, multi-map mapsets) that produces the SYMBOLIC-MAP layout (offsets/lengths matching the generated COBOL copybook field structure), so SEND/RECEIVE MAP exercise REAL maps loaded from app/bms instead of stubs. Likely should align with / derive from the symbolic copybook (cpy-bms/*.CPY) which our COBOL layout engine already parses, rather than re-deriving from the BMS macro. Cross-check the two.

IMPACT: blocks faithful end-to-end CICS emulation (real screens). Currently every CICS test uses stub maps. Surfaced while extending the durable real-CardDemo test to COACTVWC turn 4 (map CACTVWA). Related: red-dragon-pz9g.5 (BMS Screen Engine), red-dragon-pz9g.10 (symbolic maps).

The plan included a fallback: 'If bms-tools is not available as a public submodule, use a minimal stub.' The shipped implementation took the FALLBACK — no vendor/, no submodule (.gitmodules has only proleap), just the inline regex _parse_bms_file in interpreter/cics/bms/loader.py. The specified repo MikeB-ACS/bms-tools no longer resolves (deleted/renamed/private) and is not on PyPI; web search finds no maintained 'bms-tools' parser (only mainframed/ANSi2BMS, a generator). So the proper-grammar path was never realized and the fallback stub can't parse real BMS.

CANDIDATE FIX DIRECTIONS (decide):
(A) Write our own proper BMS grammar (Lark) in-repo: DFHMSD/DFHMDI/DFHMDF, col-72 continuations, arbitrary param order, multi-map mapsets, ATTRB/OCCURS/PICIN/PICOUT. Produces map field layout. We own it; consistent with the CICS command Lark grammar.

SEND/RECEIVE MAP read <base>O/<base>I from that group, so the symbolic-map offsets/lengths are exactly what's needed; screen POS/ATTRB (only in the .bms macro) are not needed for value-level field extraction. Eliminates the regex parser entirely.

title: CICS SEND/RECEIVE MAP: MAP()/MAPSET() data-name operands lowered as literal Const, not resolved to runtime value
description:
SEND MAP / RECEIVE MAP lowering in interpreter/cics/strategy.py (~445-450 for SEND, ~RECEIVE path) emits the MAP and MAPSET operands as hardcoded literal Const(value=opts.get('MAP',...)). When the operand is a quoted literal (MAP('COSGN0A')) this happens to work, but when it is a DATA-NAME (MAP(CCARD-NEXT-MAP) / MAP(LIT-THISMAP)) the literal STRING 'CCARD-NEXT-MAP' is passed to the BMS loader instead of the field's runtime value ('CACTVWA'), so loader.get() misses, the screen builtin takes the unknown-map branch, and no symbolic <base>O fields are emitted (empty screen fields).

This is the standard CardDemo screen idiom (MOVE LIT-THISMAP TO CCARD-NEXT-MAP; SEND MAP(CCARD-NEXT-MAP)), so it blocks every CardDemo screen program beyond the two sign-on/menu programs that use literal map names. Surfaced driving real COACTVWC turn 4 (COACTVWC.cbl:583 SEND, :611 RECEIVE).

FIX: replace the two Const emits with emit_operand_value(ctx, opts.get('MAP'/'MAPSET'), materialised) (strategy.py:93) which already strips quotes for literals AND resolves data-names via ctx.resolve_field_ref + emit_decode_field -- exactly as XCTL PROGRAM (strategy.py:400) and READ FILE (508,563) do. Apply to BOTH SEND MAP and RECEIVE MAP (MAP + MAPSET operands). CICS-layer only; do NOT touch core (vm/ir/run/executor).

TDD: unit test that SEND/RECEIVE MAP with a data-name operand resolves to its runtime value (mirror tests/unit/cics/test_operand_value.py style); integration test: COBOL program MOVEs a map name into WS then SEND MAP(WS-VAR) and assert the screen carries the resolved map name + a field. After fix, the real COACTVWC turn 4 renders CACTVWA.
close_reason: Stale — already fixed. cics/strategy.py:699 resolves MAP()/MAPSET() operands via emit_operand_value (present since the interpreter/cics/ -> cics/ migration, commit 2a5922f, which postdates this issue). Verified live: tests/integration/cics/test_region_e2e.py::test_send_map_data_name_resolves_runtime_value (docstring cites g5gx) passes; full 66-test tests/integration/cics/ suite passes under JDK 17.

title: CICS: subscripted option operand resolves to element 1 (emit_operand_value drops the subscript offset)
description:
XCTL PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) (and any subscripted CICS option operand) resolves to the FIRST table element, not the indexed one. The CICS parser captures the subscripted text (pz9g.18) and the COBOL frontend's uniform resolver already handles it: emit_operand_value -> ctx.resolve_field_ref -> parse_subscript_notation splits NAME(SUB), resolves the base, and computes the element offset into ref.offset_reg. But emit_operand_value (interpreter/cics/strategy.py) calls ctx.emit_decode_field(region_reg, ref.fl) WITHOUT ref.offset_reg, so emit_decode_field falls back to the base field offset (element 1) and the subscript is ignored.

Fix: pass ref.offset_reg -> ctx.emit_decode_field(region_reg, ref.fl, ref.offset_reg). One line; routes the operand straight from parser through the uniform COBOL field resolver (no CICS-layer subscript special-casing). Affects all operands resolved via emit_operand_value (RETURN TRANSID, XCTL PROGRAM, VSAM FILE/DATASET) uniformly. Bare (non-subscripted) operands are unaffected (their offset_reg is the base offset). Surfaced extending the real CardDemo flow to a menu option selection (COMEN01C XCTLs PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION))).
acceptance_criteria: XCTL PROGRAM(TBL(IDX)) resolves to the value of element IDX (e.g. element 2 = 'COADM01C'); RETURN TRANSID and VSAM FILE/DATASET subscripted operands likewise; bare operands still work.
close_reason: emit_operand_value now passes ref.offset_reg to emit_decode_field, so subscripted CICS operands (XCTL PROGRAM(WS-PGM(WS-IDX)) etc.) resolve the indexed element via the COBOL frontend's uniform resolve_field_ref. One-line fix, no CICS-layer subscript logic. JAR-gated test asserts element 2 resolves; full suite green.

title: CICS parser: subscripted option value PROGRAM(X(idx)) + NOHANDLE flag not parsed
description:
The Lark CICS command parser (interpreter/cics/cics_parser.py) fails on an option value that is a SUBSCRIPTED data-name with nested parentheses, e.g.:
    EXEC CICS INQUIRE PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) NOHANDLE
ValueError: Cannot parse EXEC CICS text: 'INQUIRE PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) NOHANDLE'. The grammar treats '(' .. ')' as the option-value delimiter, so the inner ')' of the subscript closes the option early and the rest ('(WS-OPTION)) NOHANDLE') is unparseable. Also NOHANDLE is a bare flag keyword that must be accepted.

Surfaced extending the real CardDemo flow to the menu: COMEN01C (transid CM00) uses option-table lookups  and won't even COMPILE today.

Fix: extend the CICS command grammar so an option value may contain balanced nested parentheses (a subscripted reference), and accept NOHANDLE (and likely other bare flags) as a flag option. Scope: cics_parser.py grammar + tests; CICS layer only. NOTE: a subscripted option operand also needs downstream resolution at lowering (XCTL/INQUIRE PROGRAM(table(idx))) — resolve the subscripted data-name to its runtime value, like the OF-qualified/leaf-name work; may be a follow-up once parsing works.
acceptance_criteria: EXEC CICS INQUIRE PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) NOHANDLE parses (verb INQUIRE, option PROGRAM with the subscripted operand text, NOHANDLE flag); COMEN01C compiles. Simple option values still parse.
close_reason: CICS grammar now parses subscripted option values via a recursive value/value_part rule (balanced nested parens, no regex balancing); NOHANDLE flag parses. 16 parser tests, full CICS suite green. Pure-Python (no JAR). NOTE: downstream resolution of a subscripted option operand (e.g. INQUIRE/XCTL PROGRAM(table(idx))) to its runtime value may be a follow-up.

title: COBOL: intrinsic FUNCTION argument that is an OF-qualified data-name is getText-concatenated, not resolved
description:
FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI OF COSGN0AI) operates on the mangled field-name text instead of the field's value. Diagnostic (real COSGN00C sign-on): the READ RIDFLD key came out as EBCDIC 'USERIDIO' = getText('USERIDI OF COSGN0AI') = 'USERIDIOFCOSGN0AI' truncated to the 8-char key field, instead of the value 'USER0001'. So UPPER-CASE upper-cased the concatenated qualified-name text, not the operand.

Root cause: the 8eiq bridge function-argument serialization (StatementSerializer.java serializeFunctionArg / serializeFunctionNode*, added in red-dragon-8eiq) does NOT structurally resolve a qualified (OF/IN) data-name argument to its leaf field reference — it falls back to a getText()-style concatenation. A simple-field arg (FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(WS-X)) works; an OF-qualified arg does not.

Fix: serialize each function argument as a structured operand using the same data-reference extraction the rest of the serializer uses (leaf name 'USERIDI', dropping the 'OF COSGN0AI' qualification — red-dragon resolves by leaf name), i.e. emit {kind:ref,name:USERIDI} (or the proper operand node) rather than concatenated text. Then the frontend's existing arg lowering decodes USERIDI to its value and UPPER-CASE works. Scope: bridge (COBOL serializer) + tests; stays in the COBOL layer, no core engine changes. This is the last known blocker before the real CardDemo sign-on READ finds the user and XCTLs to COMEN01C.
acceptance_criteria: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI OF COSGN0AI) yields the uppercased VALUE of USERIDI (e.g. 'USER0001'); the real sign-on READ key matches the seeded record. Simple-field function args still work. No core-engine edits.
close_reason: OF-qualified data-name in function/expr args now resolves to the leaf field via leafDataName() (first dataName of qualifiedDataNameFormat1) instead of getText() flattening. FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI OF COSGN0AI) -> USERIDI value. Bridge-only, no core. VERIFIED: real CardDemo sign-on (COSGN00C) now reaches XCTL to COMEN01C end-to-end.

title: CICS: READ/STARTBR DATASET(...) keyword + data-name file operand not resolved (returns RESP_DISABLED)
description:
EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-USRSEC-FILE) ... never resolves the dataset -> engine returns RESP_DISABLED (84), so the READ never consults the key and the program's EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD hits WHEN OTHER. Two defects in the VSAM lowering (interpreter/cics/strategy.py, the _VSAM_POINT_VERBS branch ~line 505 and the browse branch ~line 559):
1. KEYWORD: it reads only opts.get('FILE'). CICS allows DATASET(...) as a synonym for FILE(...). CardDemo uses DATASET. So opts.get('FILE') is None -> file_name lowered as empty/None.
2. DATA-NAME OPERAND: even with the DATASET alias, the operand WS-USRSEC-FILE is a DATA-NAME (PIC X(8) VALUE 'USRSEC  '), not a literal. The lowering currently emits Const(opts.get('FILE')) — the field NAME — instead of resolving the field's runtime VALUE. Must resolve it like RETURN TRANSID/XCTL PROGRAM did (red-dragon-pz9g.13, emit_operand_value): if the operand names a field, decode it to its runtime value; else literal. The VsamEngine already strips spaces/quotes and upper-cases, so a resolved 'USRSEC  ' matches a dataset registered as USRSEC.

Apply to READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE (FILE/DATASET) and STARTBR (FILE/DATASET). Surfaced re-spiking the real sign-on (COSGN00C reads USRSEC via DATASET(WS-USRSEC-FILE)). Confirmed: engine.read got file_name='None', keylen=8 (LENGTH OF works), RESP=84.
acceptance_criteria: READ/STARTBR/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE accept DATASET(...) as a synonym for FILE(...); a data-name file operand resolves to its runtime value (WS-USRSEC-FILE -> 'USRSEC') so the engine finds the dataset; literal file names still work.
close_reason: VSAM lowering accepts DATASET(...) as synonym for FILE(...) and resolves a data-name file operand to its runtime value via emit_operand_value. JAR-gated round-trip test with DATASET(WS-DSN). CICS-layer only, no core touch. Full suite green.

title: CICS: RETURN TRANSID / XCTL PROGRAM with a data-name operand lowers the name as a literal
description: EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) yields DispatchResult(transid='WS-TRANID') -- the field NAME -- instead of the field's VALUE ('CC00'), so the dispatcher cannot route and ABENDs TRNI. CicsLoweringStrategy.lower emits Const(value=opts.get('TRANSID')) for the RETURN/XCTL operands, always treating them as literals and never resolving a data-name to its runtime value. Same literal-only treatment applies to XCTL PROGRAM(data-name) (works only when a literal program name is used). Fix: when the TRANSID/PROGRAM operand names a data item, resolve+decode it (the F-machinery emit_copy_in / field decode) and pass the runtime value; keep the literal fast-path. strategy.py ~line 354.
acceptance_criteria: RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) routes by the field's value; XCTL PROGRAM(WS-PGM) resolves the runtime program name; literal forms still work.
close_reason: Fixed with TDD (emit_operand_value resolves data-name operands); full suite green.

title: CICS: HANDLE CONDITION/AID real semantics + EIBAID write-back
description: HANDLE CONDITION, HANDLE AID and HANDLE ABEND are all currently aliased to a single no-op builtin (__cics_handle_abend). Two real semantics are missing: (1) HANDLE CONDITION/AID must register a label and cause a branch to it after subsequent commands when the condition/AID fires; (2) EIBAID is never written into the EIB between turns — the RECEIVE MAP / dispatcher path drops the attention key. CardDemo menu navigation and program exit branch on EIBAID (e.g. IF EIBAID = DFHPF3) and on HANDLE AID, so without these, PF-key navigation does not work.
design: EIBAID: when an input event arrives (RECEIVE MAP or between pseudo-conversational turns), write its attention id into the EIB region (same mechanism as init_eib's EIBAID write). Depends on field-ref/EIB write path from pz9g.7. HANDLE: epic DESIGN prescribes 'CALL __cics_handle(...) + injected BRANCH_IF after subsequent commands; prefer normalizing to RESP-check form where CardDemo allows.' Translator records the handler label and emits conditional branches; start with the RESP-check normalization where possible, fall back to label-branch injection.
acceptance_criteria: EIBAID reflects the terminal attention key inside the program; HANDLE AID branches to the registered label on the matching key; covered by unit + integration tests.

AUDIT (18 online programs): HANDLE AID used 0x; HANDLE CONDITION used 1x (off happy path, now explicit no-op). So this story reduces to EIBAID write-back only (navigation uses IF EIBAID = DFHPFnn directly). Faithful HANDLE machinery split out as a separate deferred story; see plan 2026-06-07-cics-handle-condition-machinery.md.

title: CICS Sub-project F: EXEC CICS field-ref wiring + BY-REFERENCE copy-back
description: ROOT GAP. Implementation of sub-projects A-E lowers EXEC CICS verbs to CallFunction with Const placeholder args (empty bytes / literals). No option data-name is resolved to its field, and no output flows back. The CICS layer can route control flow (RETURN/XCTL/dispatch) but CANNOT MOVE APPLICATION DATA. This contradicts the epic's own architecture, which specifies: parse the command, resolve option data-names NAME-BASED at lowering time (resolve_field_ref against MaterialisedSectionedLayout), pass them BY REFERENCE, and let the existing CALL USING copy-back mechanism move outputs back. That copy-back machinery already shipped; the CICS lowering simply never used it.
design:
For each EXEC CICS option that names a COBOL data item (FROM, INTO, RIDFLD, COMMAREA, APPLID, SYSID, YYYYMMDD, TIME, RESP, LENGTH-as-ref, etc.): at lowering time in CicsLoweringStrategy.lower(), resolve the name against the MaterialisedSectionedLayout and emit a reference arg (address/region) instead of Const(b''). Literals stay literal. The builtin then reads inputs from the referenced region and writes outputs back into the caller's region via BY-REFERENCE copy-back (same path CALL USING uses).

Cascade fixed by this story:
- COMMAREA on RETURN TRANSID / XCTL actually carries state between turns (currently always empty).
- RESP(r) and EIBRESP written back after each call -> 'IF EIBRESP = DFHRESP(NORMAL)' checks work.
- ASSIGN APPLID/SYSID write the target field (builtin is currently a no-op).
- FORMATTIME YYYYMMDD/TIME output fields written.
- VSAM READ/WRITE INTO/FROM move record bytes; RIDFLD passes the key.
- SEND MAP loads the FROM area; RECEIVE MAP writes the INTO area.

Acceptance: a builtin receiving a referenced field can read its current bytes and a write is observable in VM memory after the call returns. Add unit tests per verb option and an integration test asserting COMMAREA round-trips across two turns.
acceptance_criteria: Field-named EXEC CICS options resolve to real field references (not Const placeholders); builtin reads/writes observable in VM memory; COMMAREA round-trips across a RETURN TRANSID turn; EIBRESP/RESP reflect the call outcome.
notes:
Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-cics-F-field-ref-wiring-design.md
Implementation plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-07-cics-F-field-ref-wiring.md. Decision locked: EIBRESP written lowering-side.

title: CICS milestone: sign-on -> menu flow end-to-end (screens/files stubbed)
description:
First proof-of-architecture milestone. With EIB fields, DFHAID/DFHBMSCA constants, and a dispatch trampoline that round-trips the COMMAREA, the COSGN00C (sign-on) -> COMEN01C/COADM01C (menu) navigation should FLOW even with screens and files stubbed.

Demonstrates the full pseudo-conversational loop without requiring full BMS or VSAM fidelity:
- First entry (EIBCALEN=0): program sends sign-on screen, RETURNs with TRANSID+COMMAREA.
- Re-entry on Enter (DFHENTER via EIBAID): PROCESS-ENTER-KEY runs; a stubbed user READ returns NORMAL; XCTL to the menu program carrying the COMMAREA.
- Menu program re-enters with the COMMAREA populated (from-program, user-id, user-type).

File READ (USRSEC) and SEND/RECEIVE MAP may be stubbed (canned record, no real screen) — the point is to prove EIB + dispatch + EXEC CICS control flow work together end-to-end. Full file/screen fidelity comes via the VSAM and BMS children.

Stubbed user READ returns NORMAL and the program XCTLs to the menu program. 4. The menu program re-enters with the COMMAREA carrying user-id/user-type set by sign-on. 5. Integration test exercises the two-transaction flow via the dispatch driver.

title: CICS command translator (grammar) + service builtins
description:
Connective tissue. Today every EXEC CICS block falls through to serializeUnknown in the ProLeap bridge -> an opaque no-op. ProLeap CAN parse it (ExecCicsStatement exists); the bridge + Python frontend must turn each verb into structured IR.

Key framing: the coupling point is RESP + data movement, not the command. A CICS program branches on the response code (IF WS-RESP-CD = DFHRESP(NORMAL) vs DFHRESP(NOTFND)) and reads what the command moved into its INTO/map fields. Get those two right and the surrounding COBOL logic executes correctly.

Fidelity tiers (19 verbs used across the 17 online programs):
- Control/state — must be real: RETURN TRANSID/COMMAREA, XCTL (delegated to the dispatch-driver child).
- File — real IF data matters: READ INTO RIDFLD, STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV/ENDBR, WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE. Move bytes into INTO target, set RESP. Backed by the VSAM-model child.
- Screen — model needed, headless OK: SEND/RECEIVE MAP. RECEIVE populates ...I fields, SEND reads ...O fields. Backed by the BMS-model child.
- Stubbable with plausible values: ASSIGN APPLID/SYSID, ASKTIME, FORMATTIME, INQUIRE.
- Control-flow sugar: HANDLE CONDITION/AID/ABEND — implement, or normalize to the RESP form at lowering.
- Terminate: ABEND.

This child covers: structured serialization of every verb (bridge), Python statement types, and the RESP-code contract + data-target movement. File and screen effects are delegated to the VSAM and BMS children.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Each EXEC CICS verb used by CardDemo parses into a structured statement (no serializeUnknown). 2. RESP/RESP2 options bind to the named fields and receive plausible response codes. 3. INTO/FROM/map data targets are populated/read. 4. Stubbable verbs (ASSIGN, ASKTIME, FORMATTIME, INQUIRE) return plausible constants. 5. ABEND terminates the transaction. 6. @covers entries for the new CICS features.
notes:
REFRAMED per epic architecture (2026-06-04): this is the CICS-command parser + object-level translator, NOT a per-verb IR lowering effort.

First task: decide parser placement (Python frontend consuming getExecCicsText, recommended; vs Java bridge). Then:
1. Hand-written parser for the CICS keyword grammar: VERB [SUBVERB] (OPTION(arg) | FLAG)*. Start with CardDemo's ~19 verbs.
2. Object-level translation: parsed command -> synthetic CallStatement (program=__cics_<verb>, USING from options: literals literal, data-names BY REFERENCE, RESP/RESP2 as BY REFERENCE out-params). Single ProLeap pass — no source rewrite.
3. SERVICE-verb bodies = builtins behind a provider (extend CobolIOProvider or sibling CicsProvider), dispatched in handlers/calls.py like __cobol_* already is. RESP via copy-back.
4. CONTROL-FLOW verbs (RETURN/XCTL/HANDLE) are NOT plain CALLs — emit builtin-call + translator-emitted IR (Return_/BRANCH). Coordinate with the dispatch-driver child (pz9g.2).
No COBOL service bodies; no new opcodes.
close_reason: Closed

title: CICS: pseudo-conversational dispatch driver (COMMAREA + RETURN/XCTL)
description:
The core architectural pattern of CICS online apps. A terminal program does NOT loop waiting for input. Instead:
1. Program builds a screen, sends it, and ENDS (EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(x) COMMAREA(y)). The task is torn down — no program in memory during think time.
2. CICS holds the COMMAREA (saved program state — e.g. CARDDEMO-COMMAREA: from/to program, current account/card/user, context flags) keyed to the TRANSID.
3. On the next keypress CICS restarts the transaction, re-runs the program from the top, and hands the COMMAREA back via the LINKAGE SECTION DFHCOMMAREA.
4. The program tests EIBCALEN=0 (fresh) vs re-entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) to know its phase.

XCTL is the other half: one-way transfer of control to another program passing the COMMAREA, with no return (sign-on -> menu -> account-view). NOT a CALL.

Build a transaction-dispatch trampoline holding {next TRANSID, COMMAREA, AID, map input}: invoke program with COMMAREA in LINKAGE; on RETURN/XCTL record next program + COMMAREA for the following iteration. Leans on the existing CALL USING/LINKAGE/persistent-WS work — the COMMAREA is conceptually a LINKAGE region passed between transactions.
acceptance_criteria: 1. EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID/COMMAREA records next transaction state and ends the program. 2. Next dispatch iteration re-enters the program with the COMMAREA in DFHCOMMAREA and correct EIBCALEN. 3. EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM/COMMAREA transfers control one-way to the named program. 4. A two-program hand-off (A XCTL B, B reads COMMAREA set by A) round-trips state correctly.
close_reason: Transaction dispatcher complete: run_cics(), _run_dispatcher_with_runner loop, parse_csd, initial_vm, flow-control lowering (RETURN/RETURN TRANSID/XCTL/ABEND). Exercised by real end-to-end flow in pz9g.9.

title: CICS: EIB fields + system copybooks (DFHAID, DFHBMSCA)
description:
Foundational, unblocks parsing of every online program. Two trivial-but-required pieces:

(1) EXEC Interface Block (EIB): CICS auto-injects a control block every program reads without declaring. CardDemo uses:
- EIBCALEN: length of received COMMAREA. 0 = first entry (no state). Universal 'am I starting fresh?' test (IF EIBCALEN = 0).
- EIBAID: which key the user pressed (Enter, PF3, PF12...). Programs EVALUATE EIBAID.
- EIBRESP/EIBRESP2: response codes (often captured via RESP() option instead).
Model the EIB as an implicit record the VM populates before each transaction (CALEN from COMMAREA length, AID from the dispatch driver input) with those names resolvable in-program.

(2) System copybooks (IBM-supplied, NOT in the CardDemo repo — expected):
- DFHAID: AID key constants DFHENTER, DFHPF1..DFHPF24, DFHCLEAR (01-level PIC X values). Compared against EIBAID.
- DFHBMSCA: BMS attribute byte constants (protected/modified/cursor/color). Set on map fields before SEND MAP.
Ship canonical versions (values are standardized) so COPY DFHAID / COPY DFHBMSCA resolve.
acceptance_criteria: 1. EIBCALEN, EIBAID, EIBRESP, EIBRESP2 are resolvable names in a parsed CICS program. 2. EIBCALEN reflects the COMMAREA length passed by the dispatch driver (0 on first entry). 3. DFHAID and DFHBMSCA copybooks resolve via COPY and expose the standard constants. 4. A program can EVALUATE EIBAID against DFHENTER/DFHPF3 and branch correctly.
close_reason: Closed

title: Run CardDemo online tier — CICS transaction environment
description:
Fitness function: execute the online (CICS) tier of AWS CardDemo (~/code/aws-mainframe-carddemo, 17 CO* programs). The interpreter supports the COBOL language core (data layout, procedure logic, CALL USING/LINKAGE/GOBACK) but none of the CICS transaction environment the online app is built on. This epic tracks the five subsystems needed to plausibly execute online transactions, plus a sign-on→menu milestone proving the architecture end-to-end.

Scope boundary: this is a CICS emulation layer, not incremental COBOL feature work. Batch programs (CBACT*/CBTRN*/CBCUS*) are a separate, smaller target (file I/O + COBOL logic, no CICS/BMS).

No implementation approach (custom vs open-source such as VBISAM/Berkeley DB/KICKS) is committed here — see individual children for the decisions to be made.
design:
ARCHITECTURE (decided 2026-06-04):

CICS is a runtime FRAMEWORK behind a provider interface, not language features. Mirrors the existing interpreter/cobol/io_provider.py pattern (COBOL file I/O already lowers OPEN/READ/WRITE to __cobol_* CALL_FUNCTION builtins dispatched to a CobolIOProvider with Null/Stub variants). CICS scales that up.

TRANSLATION STRATEGY — object-level, single ProLeap pass:
- ProLeap treats EXEC CICS as OPAQUE TEXT: ExecCicsStatement exposes only getExecCicsText(), no parsed options. So we MUST write a CICS command parser ourselves (verb + KEYWORD(arg)|FLAG grammar; ~19 verbs in CardDemo; small hand-written parser, extend incrementally).
- Translate at the OBJECT level, NOT textually: parse the command text -> construct a synthetic CallStatement (program + USING name-strings) directly. Do NOT rewrite COBOL source.
- Critically this needs only ONE ProLeap pass. A textual rewrite (IBM translator model) would force a second parse + column-correct COBOL generation. The object route avoids both because field resolution is NAME-BASED at lowering time (resolve_field_ref against MaterialisedSectionedLayout) — a synthetic CallStatement carrying correct name-strings is indistinguishable from a parsed one, and the data items it references were already parsed by ProLeap in the same pass (data division).
- Calling convention is OURS (not IBM DFHEIVxx temps): pass options directly as USING args (literals stay literal, data-names go BY REFERENCE). No scratch temps -> no data-division change -> no re-parse.

IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT — what the CALL bodies are:
- SERVICE verbs (READ/WRITE/browse/SEND-RECEIVE MAP/ASSIGN/ASKTIME/etc.) -> synthetic CALL -> existing CALL USING->IR path -> BUILTIN body behind a provider (VSAM provider, BMS provider, clock, EIB). NO COBOL service bodies, NO new opcodes. RESP flows back via BY REFERENCE copy-back (the CALL USING work already shipped).
- CONTROL-FLOW verbs are NOT plain CALLs: translator emits builtin-call (mutate dispatcher/handler state) PLUS translator-emitted IR control flow:
  * RETURN TRANSID -> CALL __cics_return(...) + Return_
  * XCTL -> CALL __cics_xctl(...) + Return_ (dispatcher invokes the target; no return)
  * HANDLE CONDITION/AID/ABEND -> CALL __cics_handle(...) + injected BRANCH_IF after subsequent commands; prefer normalizing to RESP-check form where CardDemo allows.
- Pre-lowered COBOL->IR plays NO role as a service body: services bottom out in host primitives COBOL cannot express (file store, screen buffer, clock, EIB), so a COBOL body would just CALL the builtin anyway.
- Only genuinely COBOL-level artifacts: the application programs themselves and the EIB/COMMAREA records (COBOL data, already handled).

PLACEMENT DECISION: translator in the Python frontend (parse getExecCicsText -> rewrite to CallStatement), keeping the CICS grammar beside the lowering it feeds and avoiding a Java rebuild per verb. (Bridge-side Java is the alternative.)
notes:
PREREQUISITE: red-dragon-9w64 (P0) — COPY copybook inlining is currently broken (stdin invocation lands source in system temp dir, defeating ProLeap's parent-dir copybook resolution; unresolvable COPY = hard parse failure). This blocks parsing of every copybook-using CardDemo program. Children .1/.5/.6 depend on it. Must be fixed first.

=== REAL-APP SIGN-ON BLOCKING CHAIN (2026-06-08 spike analysis) ===
Driving the real sign-on program end-to-end through run_carddemo_region surfaced a
layered set of blockers. Three already fixed (closed): hex-literal VALUE X'nn'
(DFHENTER), bridge REDEFINES/FILLER NPE (BMS symbolic maps parse), RETURN TRANSID/
XCTL PROGRAM data-name resolution (pz9g.13). Current state: real sign-on PARSES,
matches EVALUATE EIBAID WHEN DFHENTER, runs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, and RECEIVE MAP
populates USERIDI/PASSWDI. Next dead-end: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN USERIDI = SPACES OR
LOW-VALUES collapses to constant-TRUE -> always 'Please enter User ID', never reaches
READ/XCTL.

Work IN THIS ORDER (blocking priority):
  1. lu25 (P1) bridge: space-normalize EVALUATE WHEN conditions  [unblocked NOW]
  2. z31u (P1) condition lowering: kill silent-TRUE fallback; support OF-qualified,
     figurative SPACES/LOW-VALUES, abbreviated OR  [blocked by lu25]
  3. me3w (P1) multi-target MOVE  +  8eiq (P1) intrinsic FUNCTION (UPPER-CASE/
     CURRENT-DATE)  [both blocked by z31u; needed for MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(...)
     TO WS-USER-ID CDEMO-USER-ID]
  4. RE-SPIKE: expect to reach READ USRSEC -> password check (EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD,
     covered by z31u) -> XCTL COMEN01C.
Non-blocking cleanup (P2, any time): 0cci SET-88-TO-TRUE, wchi SEND TEXT continued
VALUE, pz9g.14 dispatcher RETURN-TRANSID no-timeout robustness.
Each fix is TDD'd and followed by a re-spike to find the next layer.

title: IDCAMS DEFINE CLUSTER: comma-separated RECORDSIZE()/KEYS() args not parsed
description:

and keys_param ("KEYS" "(" INT INT ")") both require space-separated integers.
Real CardDemo IDCAMS jobs frequently use comma-separated args instead:

Fix: comma should be an allowed separator between INT tokens in both

"," to the ignore pattern between digits -- the latter is broader and

title: jcl_graph.py: _step_proc_provenance mislabels proc attribute when a job has duplicate step names
description:
Discovered while verifying PlanB Task 8 (build_carddemo_graph.py real proclib wiring).

In jackal/jackal/jcl_graph.py, _step_proc_provenance() builds:
    original_by_name = {s.name.upper(): s for s in job.steps}
keyed by step name. Real CardDemo JCL (jackal/third-party/carddemo/app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl)
has two steps both literally named STEP05R:
  - line 23: //STEP05R EXEC PROC=REPROC,...
  - line 37: //STEP05R  EXEC PGM=SORT

The dict comprehension keeps only the LAST occurrence (the SORT step), so when resolving
provenance for the expanded inner step TRANREPT.STEP05R.PRC001, outer_step =
original_by_name['STEP05R'] incorrectly resolves to the SORT step instead of the REPROC
step. Result: the JOB->STEP edge to TRANREPT.STEP05R.PRC001 carries attrs={'proc': 'SORT'}
instead of the correct attrs={'proc': 'REPROC'}.

The step itself IS still correctly expanded (TRANREPT.STEP05R.PRC001 -> IDCAMS, right DDs,
right dataset), so this is a provenance-attribute-only bug, not a structural one — REPROC
no longer appears as a spurious PROGRAM node (Task 8's primary goal), but the 'proc' edge
attribute for this expansion is wrong.

Fix should key original_by_name by (name, position) or otherwise disambiguate steps that
share a name within one job, since JCL does permit step name reuse across what are
effectively unrelated step groups in some real-world jobs.

Out of scope for PlanB Task 8 (which only touches knowledge_graph/build_carddemo_graph.py) —
filed as a follow-up against jcl_graph.py / Task 6.
close_reason: Fixed: _step_proc_provenance now uses a positional walk instead of a name-keyed dict, correctly attributing each expanded PROC step to its true originating outer step even when step names repeat within a job. Commit f0a2b50d, TDD (regression test added first, verified red, then fixed). 181/181 tests pass.

title: PDS/PDSE partitioned datasets + member access (DSN=LIB(MEMBER))
description: BIGGEST structural gap surfaced by the roadmap map. A jackal dataset is a single file with no member concept; real jobs reference DSN=SOME.LIB(MEMBER) pervasively. DD without member = whole PDS (concatenation/IEBCOPY); with member = that file. Threads into allocate/resolve and the COBOL/utility provider. Interacts with DD concatenation (1o2.5) for STEPLIB chains and PROC libs (1o2.2/1o2.15).

title: Broaden IDCAMS verb coverage (bare DELETE, standalone SET, GDG define, alternate-index toolchain)
description:
v2 IDCAMS supports only: DELETE dsname CLUSTER, DEFINE CLUSTER (KSDS only), REPRO INFILE-OUTFILE, and the combined IF MAXCC op n THEN SET MAXCC = n. Audited all 21 real IDCAMS SYSIN steps in the CardDemo corpus (vendor/carddemo/app/jcl + proc) directly -- this supersedes the original description's assumed scope (LISTCAT, PRINT, REPRO FROMKEY/TOKEY/COUNT/SKIP, EXPORT/IMPORT/VERIFY, standalone ALTER): NONE of those appear anywhere in the real corpus. Do not implement them speculatively.

Real gaps found, ranked by how many real jobs actually break on them today:

1. Bare `DELETE dsname` with NO trailing type keyword (DUSRSECJ.jcl, ESDSRRDS.jcl x2 -- 3 occurrences). delete_cmd's grammar rule hard-requires the literal CLUSTER token; this real syntax fails to parse today.
2. Standalone `SET MAXCC = 0` (not wrapped in IF...THEN) -- 8 occurrences across the corpus. Common idempotency idiom: DELETE x then unconditionally SET MAXCC=0 so a missing dataset doesn't kill the job. Grammar only knows SET as the tail of the combined if_cmd rule; a bare SET statement isn't a valid top-level command.
3. `DEFINE GENERATIONDATAGROUP (NAME() LIMIT() SCRATCH)` -- the real GDG-base-definition verb, DEFGDGB.jcl/DEFGDGD.jcl, 6+ occurrences. Directly overlaps jackal-1o2.4 (GDG) -- can't stand up the GDG bases those jobs need without this.
4. The alternate-index toolchain, always appearing together as a 4-verb sequence in CARDFILE.jcl, TRANFILE.jcl, XREFFILE.jcl, TRANIDX.jcl (4 files):
   - `DELETE dsname ALTERNATEINDEX` (not CLUSTER)
   - `DEFINE ALTERNATEINDEX (NAME() RELATE() KEYS() NONUNIQUEKEY UPGRADE RECORDSIZE() VOLUMES() CYLINDERS()) DATA() INDEX()`
   - `DEFINE PATH (NAME() PATHENTRY())`
   - `BLDINDEX INDATASET() OUTDATASET()`
   None of these four exist in grammar or executor today. This is the single biggest lift on the list -- real VSAM alternate-index machinery, not just a grammar rule.
5. `DELETE dsname CLUSTER PURGE` -- 1 occurrence (CBEXPORT.jcl). PURGE isn't a modeled trailer.
6. `IF LASTCC=12 THEN SET MAXCC=0` -- 1 file (DEFGDGB.jcl), repeated 6x within it. Two grammar gaps: LASTCC (not just MAXCC), and a bare `=` operator (not the EQ keyword).

Confirmed ZERO real usage in the corpus (do not build speculatively): LISTCAT, PRINT, VERIFY, standalone ALTER (non-ALTERNATEINDEX), REPRO with FROMKEY/TOKEY/COUNT/SKIP, EXPORT/IMPORT as IDCAMS verbs (CBEXPORT/CBIMPORT are COBOL program names, not IDCAMS verbs -- false positive from a naive grep).

Parsing is not the whole job: jackal/jackal/idcams/executor.py only wires Delete/DefineCluster(KSDS-only)/Repro/IfMaxcc into the real DatasetCatalog/VSAM driver. Items 3 and 4 each need real catalog/VSAM-engine execution semantics added, not just a grammar rule.
design:
Suggested slicing, smallest/highest-leverage first:
  a. Bare DELETE + standalone SET (items 1+2) -- pure grammar fixes, unblocks 3 files outright, no executor changes needed (Delete/IfMaxcc handlers already exist, just need the grammar to recognize the bare forms).
  b. DEFINE GENERATIONDATAGROUP (item 3) -- ties directly into jackal-1o2.4 GDG work; do alongside or right after that epic child.
  c. IF LASTCC=n / bare `=` operator (item 6) -- small grammar extension, single file but repeated.
  d. DELETE ... CLUSTER PURGE (item 5) -- trivial trailer addition.
  e. Alternate-index toolchain (item 4) -- biggest lift, real VSAM AIX execution semantics, should be its own follow-up/sub-issue, not bundled with (a)-(d).
Audited directly against vendor/carddemo/app/jcl/*.jcl + proc/*.prc SYSIN blocks (grep + manual read), not inferred from the bead's original text.

title: DD concatenation (multiple datasets under one DDname)

Add: grammar for the unnamed-continuation DD form; model a DD as carrying an ordered list of datasets; sequential reads span the concatenation in order.

Model: DD.datasets: tuple[...] (or a Concatenation wrapper) — preserve frozen/FP. red-dragon SequentialDriver reads must chain across members (or jackal concatenates at provide time). Interacts with STEPLIB once PROC/load-lib semantics land.

title: SORT and IEBGENER utilities

title: Implicit SYNCPOINT + cursor-close at pseudo-conversational RETURN
description: At a pseudo-conversational RETURN (TRANSID), model CICS task-end: commit the unit of work (rollback on abend) and close all DB2 cursors, resetting the SQL session per turn. WHY: squall's session (cursors/connection) lives in the module-global Builtins.TABLE __exec_sql closure, NOT in VM state. cicada re-invokes run_cics with a fresh VMState per turn but the SAME Builtins.TABLE, so the session persists across turns — leaking turn-1 cursors into turn-2, the opposite of CICS (each pseudo-conversational turn closes cursors and releases the DB2 thread). True conversational (one continuous run, no RETURN boundary) correctly preserves the session, so the fix keys on the RETURN. The RedDragon suspend/resume continuation (ExecutionState) holds only VM state, never Builtins.TABLE, so the session is never part of resumable state regardless of in-process vs serialized resume. MECHANISM: cicada's RETURN lowering emits a call to a named squall session-end builtin (no cics<->squall import; same name-convention composition as Builtins.TABLE / the strategy registry); no-op if DB2/squall not wired. DEPENDS ON the squall __sql_session_end builtin.

title: __sql_session_end builtin: close all cursors + SYNCPOINT (reset SQL session)
description: Expose a named builtin (e.g. __sql_session_end) that closes all open cursors and SYNCPOINTs the unit of work (commit on normal end, rollback on abend). This is the squall-side hook cicada calls at a pseudo-conversational RETURN to reset the SQL session per turn — modelling real CICS task-end (implicit SYNCPOINT + cursor close at thread dealloc, incl. WITH HOLD). Standalone squall never calls it; it exists for the cicada+DB2 compose. Small: reuse the cursor-registry close + the COMMIT/ROLLBACK already built (618ddf5). Composition is name-convention only (no cics<->squall import).

title: Typed validation: data_layout category must agree with dclgen sql_type (fail loud)

When binding a host var that carries dclgen field_meta, validate that ProLeap's data_layout category agrees with the recorded dclgen category/sql_type, and fail LOUD on mismatch — catching copybook/schema drift (e.g. dclgen generated BINARY but the inlined copybook parsed as something else, or a VARCHAR group is missing its -LEN/-TEXT children). For VARCHAR: assert the len_var child is BINARY and the text_var child is ALPHANUMERIC. For scalar kinds: assert data_layout[host_var].category == dclgen category. Runs where data_layout is available (bind time / first builtin run). TDD: a deliberately-mismatched sidecar must raise. No existing fields mismatch, so it is additive.

title: WHENEVER SQLERROR / SQLWARN: program-controlled error branching
description: Surfaced reviewing Db2Backend error handling. Today a SQL failure sets a (now real) negative SQLCODE and execution continues — faithful to the DEFAULT 'WHENEVER SQLERROR CONTINUE'. But real embedded SQL lets a program declare 'EXEC SQL WHENEVER SQLERROR GOTO handler' / 'PERFORM' / 'STOP', and the precompiler then auto-inserts a SQLCODE check+branch after every EXEC SQL statement. Implement WHENEVER (SQLERROR/SQLWARN/NOT FOUND -> CONTINUE/GOTO/PERFORM) so a program can opt into automatic error branching/halting instead of hand-checking SQLCODE. This is the 'should it halt on errors' mechanism: the backend stays faithful (SQLCODE + continue); WHENEVER is where halting/branching is expressed, program-controlled. Faithful numeric SQLCODE (get_sqlcode) already landed (bbfd4f7).
close_reason: Slice 1 shipped: WHENEVER SQLERROR (<0) / NOT FOUND (=100) with CONTINUE / GO TO. Implemented as a real precompiler directive — strategy keeps lexically-scoped per-condition state and lowers a synthetic IF SQLCODE <cmp> <val> GO TO target via ctx.lower_statement after each non-whenever statement (reuses RedDragon IF+GOTO lowering; no raw-IR branch, no label-naming coupling). Removed the latent bug where WHENEVER lowered to a __exec_sql query. 267 tests green incl. DB2 e2e (WHENEVER SQLERROR GO TO branches to handler). SQLWARNING deferred (needs SQLWARN population / squall-ud0); PERFORM/STOP are not DB2 WHENEVER actions. Found+filed a ProLeap EXEC SQL preprocessor bug in red-dragon (underscore/literal patterns -> 'missing END_EXEC').

title: Endianness-aware binary codec (COMP big-endian vs COMP-5 native)
description: squall's SQLCA is standardized on COMP (big-endian) and squall's _binary codec is big-endian — self-consistent in the closed squall+RedDragon system (no real Db2 wire to match), which is why the static.sqb SQLCA (SQLCODE=0) round-trips fine. But db2-samples DATA host vars are often COMP-5 (native/little-endian). If RedDragon decodes COMP-5 as little-endian while squall's codec is big-endian, a COMP-5 numeric host var would mismatch. Verify RedDragon's COMP-5 handling and, if it differs from COMP, make _binary_decode/_binary_encode honor the field's endianness (COMP vs COMP-5) per data_layout. Trigger: the first testbed program that binds a non-zero COMP-5 numeric host var.
close_reason: Investigated for criticality: COMP-5 endianness is a NON-issue. squall's binary codec round-trips COMP-5 self-consistently (big-endian), and RedDragon maps COMP-5 -> BINARY -> big-endian too, so values are correct. The observed cursor.sqb symptom (dept not displaying) was NOT COMP-5: it was a RedDragon multi-operand DISPLAY bug (only the first operand emitted) — filed + fixed as red-dragon-8g6r (e6fe21c7), bumped here in ddd30c8. cursor.sqb now displays 'SANDERS  in dept. 20 is a manager' etc. No squall-side change needed for COMP-5.

title: Faithful CONNECT: backend registry + connection lifecycle (not a no-op)
description:
CONNECT/DISCONNECT/SET CONNECTION/CONNECT RESET are currently no-ops (SQLCODE 0) because squall is handed a single pre-established SqlBackend. This discards real semantics:
- Database-name routing: CONNECT TO <name> selects WHICH database; multiple CONNECT targets collapse onto one backend today.
- Connection lifecycle: after CONNECT RESET, the next SQL should fail with SQLCODE -1024 (no connection); squall keeps working.
- Auth: USER/USING credentials are ignored.

Faithful model: squall holds a {database-name -> SqlBackend} registry. CONNECT TO <name> looks up + sets the ACTIVE backend; SET CONNECTION switches; CONNECT RESET clears; SQL before any connect / after reset returns -1024. The single-backend case becomes a one-entry registry with an implicit connect. Fine to defer while the testbed is single-database (CONNECT TO sample), but needed for multi-DB / lifecycle fidelity.
close_reason: Faithful CONNECT shipped: name->backend registry, per-run connection lifecycle (always-disconnected start; -1024 no-connection / -1013 unknown-db / -1338 not-established), idempotent re-connect with ignored USER/USING creds (testbed double-CONNECT idiom), CONNECT TO / SET CONNECTION / DISCONNECT / CONNECT RESET. Structured CONNECT grammar (no catch-all value-matching). 261 tests green incl. two-real-DB2-database routing e2e (MOJO+MOJO2). Out of scope (not regressions): credential validation, two-phase commit, cicada pseudo-conversational reset (cicada-6hv/squall-ipq).

title: Tolerant host-var/column type coercion (convert + SQLWARN + indicator)
description:
The coercion layer currently fails strict: any host-var (PIC-derived) type vs column (metadata) type mismatch aborts the statement with a genuine-failure SQLCODE (-301), writing nothing. This issue tracks making it tolerant, matching production DB2 SQL assignment rules:

- Bucket 1 (convertible, lossless): silently convert across compatible types (numeric<->numeric, DATE<->CHAR, narrowing into wider fields). SQLCODE 0.
- Bucket 2 (convertible, lossy): convert WITH a diagnostic. String truncation -> keep SQLCODE 0, set SQLWARN1='W', and if an indicator variable is supplied set it to the ORIGINAL (pre-truncation) length. Numeric fractional truncation behaves analogously.
- Bucket 3 (won't fit / incompatible): the genuine failures the strict layer already returns, refined to the right codes — -304 (value out of range for host var on fetch), -302 (input host var out of range for column), -301 (incompatible data type).

Depends on: the NULL-indicator host-var plumbing (:VAR:IND) being threaded through binding, since bucket-2 truncation reporting uses the indicator. The strict coercion seam built now is the branch point this fills in.

title: EXEC CICS LINK + logical-level stacking (suspend across LINK)
description:
Support EXEC CICS LINK (call-with-return across CICS programs) and make a
conversational task suspend/resume correctly when it suspends INSIDE a LINKed
sub-program. Last substantial piece of the conversational design deck
(docs/design/conversational-suspend-resume.html; red-dragon
docs/notes-on-vm-design.md#cooperative-suspendresume).

== WHAT LINK IS ==
CICS program control has three verbs:
  - XCTL: transfer, NO return (caller is replaced). CardDemo navigates by XCTL.
  - LINK: call a separate CICS program at a NEW logical level; callee has its own
    working storage + EIB + a passed COMMAREA (copy-in/copy-out); on the callee's
    EXEC CICS RETURN, control comes BACK to the caller after the LINK.
  - RETURN: pop one logical level.
CICS keeps a per-task logical-level stack (terminal=1; each LINK pushes, each
RETURN pops; XCTL replaces). Distinct from COBOL CALL: CALL frames live in one
VMState's call_stack (already handled — suspend/resume across nested CALL is
tested 1+2 deep); LINK crosses the CICS-program boundary, which cicada models as
separate run_cics / LinkedProgram executions.

== CURRENT STATE ==
NOT modeled at all. cics/types.py DispatchKind = {RETURN, RETURN_TRANSID, XCTL,
ABEND} — no LINK. Corpus scan (whitespace-normalised, comments stripped): ZERO
EXEC CICS LINK in all 29 CardDemo programs and zBANK; CardDemo uses EXEC CICS
XCTL (17 programs). So nothing currently exercises LINK and nothing is blocked.

== TWO LAYERS ==
  Layer 1 - LINK at all (pseudo-conversational): add DispatchKind.LINK; the
    strategy lowers EXEC CICS LINK to a dispatch result; the dispatcher runs the
    callee (separate program) with COMMAREA copy-in, then copy-out on the callee's
    RETURN, and resumes the caller after the LINK. Plain A->LINK->B->RETURN pair
    tests this.
  Layer 2 - suspend ACROSS LINK (conversational): the task's continuation becomes
    a STACK of ExecutionStates (one per logical level), owned by the dispatcher as
    a first-class Task. When a LINKed callee suspends at RECEIVE, freeze the
    callee's ExecutionState; the caller is already frozen at its LINK call site.
    Resume the leaf; on its RETURN, pop to the caller, hand back the COMMAREA,
    resume the caller after the LINK. Keep each level's VMState (with its own
    COBOL call_stack) separate; marshal COMMAREA at the boundary (do NOT merge
    into one VMState — preserves CICS semantics and avoids region aliasing).

== TESTBED (researched) ==
Real source: cicsdev/cics-banking-sample-application-cbsa (CBSA). Uses LINK
extensively and realistically, incl. NESTED LINKs (BNK1CAC->CREACC->INQCUST/
INQACCCU; DELCUS->DELACC/INQACCCU) and a pervasive abend-handler LINK
PROGRAM(WS-ABEND-PGM).
CONSTRAINT: most business-logic callees use EXEC SQL (Db2) — CREACC, INQACC,
DELACC, XFRFUN, CRECUST, DBCRFUN, INQACCCU, etc. cicada has NO Db2/EXEC SQL
support, so those won't run. SQL-free programs are the BMS UI shells (which LINK
into the Db2 programs) plus leaf utilities. No SQL-free program LINKs another
SQL-free one, so there is NO off-the-shelf fully-runnable caller->callee(->suspend)
chain in CBSA.
USABLE REAL CALLEES (SQL/BMS/VSAM-free, perfect LINK callees):
  - GETCOMPY (43 lines): LINKAGE DFHCOMMAREA (company-name x(40)); MOVE 'CICS Bank
    Sample Application' TO COMPANY-NAME; EXEC CICS RETURN. COPY GETCOMPY copybook
    (cobol_copy/GETCOMPY.cpy) = 03 GETCompanyOperation / 06 company-name pic x(40).
  - GETSCODE (46 lines): same shape, returns a sort code.

== RECOMMENDED PLAN (zBANK-style: real callee + minimal caller) ==
  1. Vendor GETCOMPY (+ GETSCODE) and their COMMAREA copybook(s) unchanged as a
     fixture (tests/integration/cics/fixtures/cbsa or similar).
  2. Layer 1: write a minimal caller A that EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('GETCOMPY')
     COMMAREA(WS) and uses the returned COMPANY-NAME; implement DispatchKind.LINK +
     COMMAREA marshaling in the dispatcher; assert A sees 'CICS Bank Sample
     Application'. TDD.
  3. Layer 2: a conversational caller that LINKs a callee which RECEIVEs (zBANK-
     style) and suspends; build the dispatcher logical-level Task stack of
     ExecutionStates; assert suspend captures both levels and resume unwinds
     correctly (mirror test_suspend_resume_calls.py but across CICS LINK rather
     than COBOL CALL).

NOTE: the underlying VM suspend/resume primitive (red-dragon SUSPEND/ExecutionState/
run_resumable/resume + run_linked_resumable/resume_linked) is DONE and exhaustively
tested incl. nested COBOL CALL; Layer 2 reuses it per logical level. Phase 3 core
(conversational RECEIVE -> SUSPEND, greenlet retired) is DONE (cicada 467ec27).
CBSA clone used for research was /tmp/cbsa (re-clone: git clone --depth 1
https://github.com/cicsdev/cics-banking-sample-application-cbsa).

title: EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD is never dispatched (verb-key mismatch)
description:
CORPT00C submits a JCL deck via EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD QUEUE('JOBS') FROM(JCL-RECORD), but cicada never dispatches it.

Root cause: the Lark EXEC CICS grammar surfaces the statement as stmt.verb == 'WRITEQ' (with 'TD' as an option keyword), while cics/strategy.py:_SYS_VERBS only registers the composite key 'WRITEQ TD'. _SYS_VERBS.get('WRITEQ') -> None, so the verb falls through to 'unimplemented verb, no IR emitted' (strategy.py:789). The submission loop runs but enqueues nothing; td_queue stays empty.

Two parts to a fix:
1. Dispatch: match verb=='WRITEQ' with a 'TD' option (like READ/WRITE handle their option keywords) -> __cics_writeq_td. (Symmetrically, a future READQ TD would need the same.)
2. Operands: the generic _SYS_VERBS path calls the builtin with args=() , so even once dispatched the QUEUE/FROM operands are dropped. make_writeq_td_builtin already accepts (data, queue_name) (see tests/unit/cics/test_system_builtins.py::test_writeq_td_appends_to_queue); the strategy must LoadRegion the FROM operand and pass the QUEUE name so real JCL/queue content is captured.

Current behaviour is pinned by tests/integration/cics/test_carddemo_reports.py (asserts the screen-first success message + td_queue == []). When fixed, that test should assert the JCL deck (~17 lines) was enqueued to 'JOBS'.

Scope: cics/ runtime only (strategy + builtin); no RedDragon/VM change. The grammar already parses the statement fine.
close_reason: Fixed: WRITEQ TD's dispatch-mismatch half was already resolved by the ANTLR4 grammar migration (WriteqTd rule -> composite verb string 'WRITEQ TD', matches _SYS_VERBS cleanly). The remaining operand-dropping bug is fixed: WRITEQ TD is now lowered in its own explicit block in cics/strategy.py (pulled out of the generic no-operand _SYS_VERBS dispatch), resolving QUEUE and FROM via emit_operand_value and passing them as real CallFunction args. TDD: unit test (tests/unit/cics/test_strategy_screen.py::test_writeq_td_lowers_with_real_args) + strengthened real-COBOL integration test (tests/integration/cics/test_carddemo_reports.py::test_real_carddemo_custom_report_submitted), both verified to fail without the fix. RESP/RESP2 writeback (a separate bug found at the same call site) is intentionally out of scope, tracked as cicada-y6l.

title: Field-to-field numeric MOVE loses fractional digits (decode→string coercion)
description:
MOVE of a numeric-DISPLAY field into another numeric field drops the fractional part. E.g. WS-SRC PIC S9(9)V99 VALUE 12345.67; MOVE WS-SRC TO WS-DST (also S9(9)V99) stores 12345.00, losing .67.

Root cause: in lower_move, the source is decoded (emit_decode_field yields the correct float 12345.67 — verified by running build_decode_zoned_ir in isolation) then converted via emit_to_string. But in the full pipeline the decoded register value is coerced from float to int before str() is called (no int() builtin call occurs; the runtime division 1234567/100 correctly yields 12345.67, yet str receives int 12345). The coercion appears to come from the VM type environment (_coerce_value / coerce_local_update in interpreter/vm/vm.py) inferring the decode-result register as Int.

Reproduces on clean code (independent of the numeric-editing / edit_picture work). A LITERAL source (MOVE 12345.67 TO WS-DST) is NOT affected — it preserves the fraction — because it skips the field decode path.

Impact: any field-to-field MOVE of fractional values; also blocks full fractional fidelity when MOVEing a numeric field into a numeric-edited item.

title: Fix condition_lowering: DFHAID values unusable as comparison operands in compound IF
description:
In COTRN00C (and likely other CICS programs), DFHAID constants appear as comparison values in compound IF conditions:

  IF EIBAID NOT = DFHENTER AND DFHPF7 AND DFHPF3
  IF EIBAID NOT = DFHENTER AND DFHPF8

condition_lowering.py cannot resolve DFHPF3/DFHPF7/DFHPF8 as comparison values in this context and logs 'unparseable condition — never matching', causing the sub-clauses to evaluate as always-false. The full condition collapses to FALSE for all EIBAID values.

Observed impact: in COTRN00C's PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD, the skip-one-READNEXT guard never fires. Page-forward (PF8) therefore starts the browse AT CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST instead of past it, producing a one-record overlap between pages. Pinned as a regression baseline in test_real_carddemo_transaction_list_page_forward.

Fix should make condition_lowering resolve DFHAID PIC X VALUE literals (defined in DFHAID.cpy) correctly when they appear as the right-hand operand in a compound relational condition.
notes: Fixed in condition_lowering.py: added _extract_implied_relation helper and abbreviated-condition repair in _lower_condition_node. ProLeap mis-serialises abbreviated operands as {condition_name: X} when X is not level-88; fix detects this and reconstructs the full relation using the inherited subject/op from the left subtree. test_real_carddemo_transaction_list_page_forward updated to assert correct pagination.

title: CICS dispatcher: peek (don't consume) input queue for EIBAID so RECEIVE MAP still gets the event
description: When the full autonomous _run_dispatcher_with_runner is written, reconcile terminal-input consumption: the loop must read the incoming InputEvent's eibaid BEFORE running the program (CardDemo programs test EIBAID / CCARD-AID-PFKxx early, before any RECEIVE MAP), but must NOT consume the event, because the program's RECEIVE MAP builtin then input_queue.get()s the same event for its field values (+ eibaid). Today _run_dispatcher_with_runner does its own input_queue.get() for the next context's eibaid, which competes with RECEIVE MAP for the same queue (latent double-consume if a program RECEIVEs). Fix: peek the next event non-destructively (queue.Queue has no peek -> add a small peekable queue wrapper, or use q.queue[0] under the lock / a deque) to set context.eibaid, leaving the event for RECEIVE MAP to consume. The per-turn CicsRegion API (interpreter/cics/dispatcher.py, added 67b3a0e2) already has the single-consume property the manual way: the caller passes the InputEvent once, the region sets context.eibaid from it AND puts it on the queue for RECEIVE; CicsRegion deliberately does NOT replicate the loop's separate get(). peek() is the autonomous-loop analog. Tie this into the deferred full-dispatcher work. Note for design: an InputEvent currently carries BOTH eibaid and fields and is consumed once by RECEIVE — the loop should treat that single event as the terminal input, not pull a second one.
